summary: Ten recorded calls, nine with learnings, agree on where the time goes: not in interpretation or modelling, but in getting field sheets, scanned logs and lab certificates into a table someone can trust. The E4 pains come from design-side geologists, a small drilling firm, mining and exploration geologists and a rail design manager, and they repeat across construction and mining: data arrives as PDF in almost every case, each lab uses its own layout, OCR mangles scans, logs carry errors that only a geologist's eye catches, and the checked data then has to be redrawn by hand. The one E5 is a data pack promised by a small drilling firm. The evidence is thin on who pays and how much: a client-side manager doubts anyone would buy a validation tool, and no specialist contractor has been interviewed for the tender-check angle.

icps.name: Engineering geologist between field and design
icps.segment: Small and mid-size ground investigation firms and the geotechnical teams of design consultancies, Italy, Greece, UK and Iberia; mining resource geologists share the same workflow
icps.who: The geologist or geotechnical engineer who receives drilling records, core photos and lab certificates from crews and labs, checks them, and turns them into the tables, logs and sections a designer works from.
icps.trigger: A campaign closes and a batch of field sheets, scans and certificates lands, or a project inherits archive boreholes that exist only on paper.
jobs: Get every borehole value out of PDFs and scans into one table
Catch the errors in third-party logs before they become design parameters
Produce logs, sections and the report tables without redrawing them
Hand the designer data in the format the calculation needs
icps.notes: E4 pains from a design consultancy's geologists, a small drilling firm, two mining geologists and a slate producer; the drilling firm owner promised a data pack (E5). Buyer and budget are untested: the geologists must ask their managers before sharing data.

journeys.title: From field records to data a designer can use
journeys.question: Can Corestone own the step between messy field and lab documents and the first table a geologist trusts, and is that step worth paying for?

stages.name: Drill and log in the field

asis.text: Crews log on paper sheets at the rig and photograph core boxes on a phone
Remote sites with no power or signal log by hand; someone retypes it into Excel later
A logging vendor puts manual entry at about 30 minutes per log (vendor claim)

pains.text: Field sheets come back in handwriting that is hard or impossible to read
Core photos arrive tilted, reversed, feet in frame, boxes filled right to left

quotes.text: mi fa paura la scrittura di gallina dei vari utenti
quotes.who: Owner, small drilling and ground investigation firm, Italy

quotes.text: normalmente si vede la foto con i piedi dentro, la foto inclinata, la foto fatta a rovescio.
quotes.who: Owner, small drilling and ground investigation firm, Italy

quotes.text: généralement ça se fait à la main, et après il y a derrière les ressources géologistes ou une personne qui pourrait s'occuper pour refaire ça sur Excel.
quotes.who: Resource geologist, quarry and mining modelling consultant

ideas.text: A capture guide and a cheap fixed rig: every box shot nadiral, same light, with a colour card
ideas.why: The drilling firm owner proposed it himself and offered to 3D print the holder

tobe.text: Crews shoot each box the same way; sheets and photos land in one project inbox

asis.text: Labs send certificates as PDFs, often scans, each lab in its own layout
Each survey method returns its own list: georadar, geoelectric, in-situ tests

pains.text: Almost all incoming data is PDF; a real database is rare
Every lab has its own certificate layout, so scripts written for one break on the next

quotes.text: Nella stramaggioranza dei casi, e direi il 99% dei casi, PDF.
quotes.who: Geologist, geotechnical team of an international design consultancy, Italy

quotes.text: Se il laboratorio A dopo 6 mesi cambia il formato del suo certificato, la procedura scritta 6 mesi prima non funziona più.
quotes.who: Geologist, geotechnical team of an international design consultancy, Italy

quotes.text: we receive more likely PDFs and we are trying with the, directly with the expert to understand because depending on experience, sometimes we cannot read the results.
quotes.who: Infrastructure project manager, rail design consultancy, Greece

ideas.text: A certificate reader that does not depend on layout, tuned on the labs a firm actually uses
ideas.why: Layout drift is what breaks the in-house scripts that exist today

tobe.text: Certificates dropped in as they come; values read whatever the lab's layout

asis.text: Values retyped into a master Excel, one tab per borehole, read by in-house Python
Bluebeam OCR helps on scans, then every number is checked again by hand
gINT support ends in 2028 and HoleBASE in 2027; users are being moved to a cloud subscription

pains.text: Extraction, not interpretation, is where most of the time goes
OCR on scans turns numbers into letters, worst on archive data
Logging software saved nothing: moving data on to Leapfrog meant going back to CSV

quotes.text: quello che ci porta via più tempo è estrarre i dati
quotes.who: Geologist, geotechnical team of an international design consultancy, Italy

quotes.text: non li prende, li prende male, il numero diventa una lettera.
quotes.who: Geotechnical data specialist, international design consultancy, Italy

quotes.text: Era mucho postproceso para meter toda la información en geo y no era inmediato el paso.
même pour un seul log, tu as minimum 4 fichiers Excel.
quotes.who: Resource geologist, quarry and mining modelling consultant

ideas.text: Batch reading of logs and certificates into one borehole table, every value linked to its page
ideas.why: The one step every call described as manual, in construction and in mining

ideas.text: Export to the firm's own Excel template, AGS 4 and the Leapfrog CSV set
ideas.why: The handoff, not the capture, is what killed the logging tool one team tried

tobe.text: One borehole table per project, written in the formats the firm already uses

asis.text: Geologists compare logs with core photos and rerun tests with their own procedures
QA/QC means going back to the paper to see what the logger actually wrote

pains.text: Errors in third-party logs are abundant, and the reviewer signs the corrections
RQD logged at 90% where the photo shows 20%, caught only by eye
Hole length differs between files and has to be traced back to photographed PDFs
UK highway AGS files pass format checks, then fail data-quality review and are reissued

quotes.text: Sì, sì, errori ce ne sono a iosa
quotes.who: Geologist, geotechnical team of an international design consultancy, Italy

quotes.text: comment tu peux mettre le RQD à 90% alors que la photo à cette profondeur-là t'as que 20%?
quand on fait du QA/QC, on part chercher dans le papier ce que la personne a dit.
quotes.who: Resource geologist, quarry and mining modelling consultant

ideas.text: A validation report: cross-file checks on depths, lengths, units and values, each flag linked to its page
ideas.why: Turns the geologist's slowest manual check into a list to accept or reject

ideas.text: A photo-based RQD and fracture estimate beside the logged value, the geologist decides
ideas.why: The 90 versus 20 case is the sharpest error heard, but RQD by eye is where incumbents already are

tobe.text: Every inconsistency listed with its source; accepted or corrected, and the change recorded

stages.name: Draw logs, sections and the report

asis.text: Stratigraphic columns drawn in AutoCAD, or written to DXF by in-house scripts
Reports of 150 to 200 pages assembled by hand from tables and charts

pains.text: Most practitioners draw columns in AutoCAD, a tool not made for it
Assembling tables and charts into long reports is slow
On Eng-Tips, small firms say gINT costs too much and fall back to Excel logs and AutoCAD fences

quotes.text: diciamo che il 90% degli utenti usa in maniera impropria AutoCAD.
quotes.who: Owner, small drilling and ground investigation firm, Italy

quotes.text: report che solitamente sono anche molto lunghi. 150-200 pagine, 1000.
quotes.who: Geologist, geotechnical team of an international design consultancy, Italy

ideas.text: Logs and sections generated as DXF from the checked table, with core photos beside each column
ideas.why: Both the drilling firm and the design team named the drawing step, and one wants photos on the log

ideas.text: A draft factual report: tables, charts and appendices pulled from the same table
ideas.why: Requested as the end state, but only after the data is trusted

tobe.text: Logs and sections redraw when a value is corrected; the report draft reads the same table

asis.text: Tunnel designers need an editable DWG longitudinal profile, not a PDF
Geotechnical and structural teams trade inputs by email across calculation rounds
Designers end up rebuilding boreholes from old PDF appendices, a data platform vendor writes

pains.text: A revised input is missed between email rounds and the calculation is rerun
Sampling happens up to a year before design; by handover the context is lost

quotes.text: So you cannot work in a PDF, you need DWG.
quotes.who: Infrastructure project manager, rail design consultancy, Greece

quotes.text: Really, it happens several times and then you have a big crash between the teams.
quotes.who: Infrastructure project manager, rail design consultancy, Greece

quotes.text: It comes too late, I forgot what he did
quotes.who: Infrastructure project manager, rail design consultancy, Greece

ideas.text: A versioned project record: the designer sees which borehole values changed since the last round
ideas.why: Missed revisions are the only E4 pain heard on the design side

tobe.text: The designer gets the DWG profile and the table from one source, with a log of changes

decisions.title: Start where the time goes: reading and checking logs and lab certificates
decisions.why: Every call with E4 pains put the hours in extraction and checking, not in modelling; one design team says interpretation is fast once the data is in.

decisions.title: Lead with a free validation report on a firm's own logs
decisions.why: It is the product, the demo and the discovery call in one, and the drilling firm has already promised a data pack to test on.

decisions.title: Write into the formats firms already use instead of asking them to move
decisions.why: A logging tool that added post-processing before Leapfrog was abandoned for CSV; the design team runs its own Excel and Python chain.

decisions.title: Keep photo RQD as an assist beside the logged value
decisions.why: The sharpest error heard is RQD by eye, but core imaging incumbents exist and one slate geologist sees little gain for his rock.

decisions.title: Do not build 3D modelling or a Leapfrog substitute
decisions.why: Advisors ruled it out, and a design team says Italian clients do not pay for 3D ground models today.

decisions.title: Test who pays before building for a buyer
decisions.why: A client-side manager doubts anyone would pay for validation and the design geologists need manager approval to share data; no contractor has been interviewed for the tender angle.
